NOTE: The Municipal Home Rule Act of 1965 prohibits municipalities from enacting ordinances covering matters which have been preempted by general law and prevents them from regulating conduct which has been made a violation of any criminal law of the state. (See 69-1018 of the Georgia Code Annotated.) What this means is that any municipal ordinance which attempts. to proscribe an act prohibited by general law is void in the absence of express constitutional or general law authorization for municipal regulation of the same act. A municipal anti-litter ordinance, for example, would be of no legal force and effect since the state has preempted the field of litter control, leaving no room for municipal regulation in the area. (See the Georgia Litter Control Law, Chapter 85-16C of the Georgia Code Annotated.)

The following list indicates some of those areas in which municipal authority has often been asserted but in which there can no longer be any valid municipal regulation due to the general law enactments cited (all references are to the Georgia Code Annotated):

Abusive or obscene language 26-2610 Bill posting Chapter 85-16D Damaging or defacing government property 26-2613 Disorderly houses 26-2614 Distributing obscene materials Ga. Laws 1975, Act 204 False fire alarm 26-2608 Fireworks control Chapter 92A-8 Gambling Chapter 26-27 Indecent exposure 26-2011 Obstructing highways, sidewalks, etc. 26-2611 Public drunkenness 99-3919 Resisting arrest 26-2505 Trespassing on or damaging private property

(Malicious mischief) 26-1503

If a municipality has on its books an ordinance proscribing any of the conduct prohibited by these general laws, then, such ordinance

el would be held to be void if its validity were challenged in a court of competent jurisdiction and the municipality were unable to point to any constitutional or general law authorization for the local enactment.

Of course, municipal Law enforcement officers are authorized to enforce state law as well as municipal law. A person may be appre- hended by municipal police officers for littering, for example, but such person must be charged with a state law violation and taken to . the county superior court rather than to the municipal court for ’ trial. The municipal court simply does not have jurisdiction to try general law offenses since its jurisdiction extends only to violations of valid municipal ordinances; i.e., ordinances dealing with subjects which have not been preempted by state law.

All of the "general offenses" included in this chapter deal with matters which have not been preempted by state law and over which municipalities can still validly exercise authority.

101 Disorderly conduct

Itt shall be unlawful for any person in the city to engage in any violent, tumultous, obstreperous, or similar disorderly conduct tending to infringe on the peace and repose of the citizens of the city. Fighting between two or more persons in which physical contact is made, except that which occurs at boxing exhibitions duly authorized by the city, shall be deemed to be disorderly conduct within the meaning of this section.

NOTE: The state's disorderly conduct statutes expressly. provide that they are not to be construed as preventing municipalities

' £rom passing or enforcing their own laws punishing disorderly conduct within their respective jurisdictions. See 26-2605 and

26-2607 of the Georgia Code Annotated. 102 Discharging firearms, air guns, etc.

It shall be unlawful for any person in the city to discharge any gun, pistol, or other firearm within 300 yards of any street, alley, or building, or at any point upon the land of another person without the express consent of the owner or occupant thereof; or to discharge at any time, any air gun, BB gun or toy gun which projects lead or any other missile.

This section shall not be construed to prohibit any officer of the law from discharging a firearm in the performance of his , duty; nor to any citizen from discharging a firearm when lawfully defending person or property.

NOTE: A person is guilty of a misdemeanor if, without legal justification, he discharges a gun or pistol on or within 50 yards of a public highway or street. See 26-2909 of the Georgia Code Annotated.

Report of treatment of wounds

All physicians and all hospital superintendents ir city are hereby required to report to the police department of the city all patients treated by physicians or diagnosed or known to be suffering from wounds inflicted by a dangerous or deadly weapon of any kind. Such report may be made in writing or by telephone, giving the name of the reporting person and the patient and any other pertinent data requested by the police department. All reports shall be made within 24 hours after treatment by a physician or after admission to the hospital.

Throwing of missiles

It shall be unlawful for any person in the city to throw any stone, rock, or other missile upon or at any vehicle, building, tree, or other public or private property, or upon or at any person in any public or private way or place.

Ballplaying

It shall be unlawful for any person to play ball by throwing, catching, pitching, or batting a bali on any public street, alley, or sidewalk of the city.

Bonfires

It shall be unlawful for any person, during a holiday or at any other time, to build a bonfire of any description within the city Limits, except at places approved and designated by the chief of the fire department.

NOTE: See also 13-102 of this Code.

Weeds

It shall be unlawful for any owner or resident of any lot, area, or place located within this municipality to permit any weeds, grass, or deleterious, unhealthful growths to obtain a height exceeding (10) inches on such property. For the purposes of this section, "weeds" shall be deemed to mean jimson, burdock, ragweed, thistle, cocklebur, dandelion, or other unsightly growths of a like kind.

- 1. Notice to remove. It shall be the duty of the (chief of police) to notify, in writing, the owner or occupant of any premises upon which weeds or other prohibited flora are permitted to grow in violation of the provisions of this section that such growths must be removed, cut, and/or destroyed within days from the date of such notice.

Notice shall be by registered mail, addressed to said owner or occupant, at his last known address.

- 2. Action upon non-compliance. Upon the failure, neglect, or refusal of any owner or occupant so notified to remove, cut, and/or destroy such weeds or other unsightly growths within the designated time period, the (director of public works) is authorized and empowered to provide for the removal, cutting, and/or destroying of such growths by or for the city.

The actual cost of such weed removal shall be assessed against the property owner upon whose premises the work is done, and, in the event the bill for such charges remains unpaid for days after it has been rendered, shall become a lien upon the premises enforceable in the same manner as provided for the collection of unpaid taxes. ,

Abandonment of motor vehicles

It shall be unlawful for any person to abandon or to Leave unattended for a period in excess of 10 days any motor vehicle on any street, road, alley, or other public way in the municipality.

NOTE: All state peace officers are authorized by general law to provide for the removal of motor vehicles which have been abandoned on any public street, road, or highway for a period of 10 days or more, and persons or firms on whose property such vehicles are towed are authorized to sell the same at public auction. See Chapter 68-23 of the Georgia Code Annotated.
